source.title: The Heavy-Tail Phenomenon in SGD
source.authors: M. Gürbüzbalaban; Umut Simsekli; Lingjiong Zhu

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Figure values are not recoverable as exact numbers from the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures SGD tail indices, including in neural networks, and discusses possible links to generalization. It does not measure train–test gaps or test any listed version’s generalization claim.
record.gate_note: The paper’s own results on tail indices are recorded because they concern a proposed property related to generalization. Generalization claims and findings attributed to cited work are not rows. Figure-only values are not reconstructed.
record.test_reason: The study proves and measures properties of SGD weight distributions, including tail-index changes with batch size, learning rate, curvature and dimension. It reports no held-out performance, train–test gaps or magnitude-aware sharpness comparisons. Its proposed connections to generalization rely on prior work and do not test V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors establish conditions for heavy-tailed stationary SGD distributions in streaming linear regression, characterize parameter dependencies, and report supporting finite-sum and neural-network tail-index experiments. Connections to generalization are proposed using prior literature; this study does not measure generalization.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes SGD tail behavior, principally through linear-regression theory and tail-index estimation; it does not reproduce the generalization interventions or measures in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The estimated tail-index varies with stepsize η, batch-size b, dimension d, variance σ, optimizer, dataset, and neural-network layer; layer trends differ.

fits_no_version.finding: Estimated tail-index decreases with increasing learning rate and decreasing batch size in synthetic regression; neural-network estimates also depend on their ratio and on layer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD weight distributions can exhibit heavy tails whose estimated thickness depends on algorithm parameters and network layer.

fits_no_version.finding: Estimated tail-index decreases as input dimension or input variance increases in Gaussian linear regression.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input dimension and curvature influence stationary tail behavior in the studied regression setup.

fits_no_version.finding: RMSProp produces mostly near-Gaussian estimates, while SVRG converges near the minimizer with an apparently degenerate stationary distribution.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizers exhibit different stationary tail behavior in the synthetic regression experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: VGG layers 1, 9 and 10 have estimated tail-indices near 2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Heavy-tail behavior is not uniform across layers of the tested VGG network.

record.problems: The neural-network experiments estimate tail indices by treating each layer as a collection of i.i.d. α-stable random variables; the paper notes layer dependence and that α may relate to η and b in a more complicated way. The reported trends rely on figures, with no numerical uncertainty reported. No train–test gap is measured.
record.rows_left_out: No applicable generalization results are reported beyond the selected tail-index and optimizer outcomes. Values for individual η, b, initialization, and layer combinations are only plotted in Figures 1–3 and are not stated numerically; the text provides grouped trend descriptions, so separate values cannot be extracted.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy and random-label chance performance.
Test error as network width increases beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected held-out performance and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under limited or broader tuning, weight decay and optimizer switching.
Large-batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and recovery through recipe changes.
Dropout effects on held-out error across dataset sizes, dropout strengths and augmentation settings.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its correlation with generalization gaps and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Test accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The cannot_determine states concern V1–V8, not the validity of the reported tail-behavior findings. Fixed iteration counts in the fully connected experiments do not constitute fixed epoch budgets when batch size varies.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label test performance.
Width sweeps and test error beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected test error and local connectivity.
Held-out performance of adaptive optimizers versus SGD.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the train–test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: linear regression, synthetic Gaussian data
rows.operation_detail: Varied stepsize η and batch-size b and estimated stationary tail-index α.
rows.value: Increasing η and decreasing b both result in decreasing α; tail-index is in strong correlation with ratio η/b.
rows.note: The text describes the trend; plotted numeric values are not supplied.
rows.check: The reported tail-index trend is supported by Section 4, but cannot establish any listed generalization effect.

rows.subject: linear regression, synthetic Gaussian data
rows.operation_detail: Varied dimension d while estimating stationary tail-index α.
rows.note: The text describes the trend; plotted numeric values are not supplied.
rows.check: Input dimension is varied in linear regression; this is not a network-width sweep with held-out error as required by V2.

rows.subject: linear regression, synthetic Gaussian data
rows.operation_detail: Varied input variance σ while estimating stationary tail-index α.
rows.note: The text describes the trend; plotted numeric values are not supplied.
rows.check: Input variance changes tail-index; neither magnitude-aware sharpness nor generalization gaps are measured.

rows.subject: RMSProp
rows.operation_detail: Estimated tail-indices in the synthetic experiment replacing SGD with RMSProp.
rows.value: The vast majority of estimated tail-indices is around 2, indicating a Gaussian behavior.
rows.note: This is a tail-behavior result, not an evaluation of generalization.
rows.check: RMSProp is an optimizer applied to synthetic linear regression, not a model subject. Near-Gaussian tail-index estimates do not measure its held-out performance relative to SGD.

rows.subject: SVRG
rows.operation_detail: Repeated the synthetic experiment with SVRG and assessed convergence near the minimizer.

conditions.value: same experiment as first synthetic experiment

rows.measure: Error from minimizer; stationary distribution behavior
rows.value: For almost all choices of η and b the algorithm converges near the minimizer (with an error in the order of 10−6); stationary distribution seems degenerate.
rows.note: The paper says this distribution does not admit a heavy-tailed behavior.
rows.check: SVRG is an optimizer applied to synthetic linear regression. Error near the minimizer, approximately 10^-6, measures optimization convergence rather than generalization.

rows.subject: fully connected neural network
rows.size_stated: three-layer network with 128 hidden units at each layer
rows.operation_detail: Varied stepsize η and batch-size b and estimated tail-index separately for each layer.
rows.value: In each layer the measured α correlate very-well with ratio η/b; dependence differs from layer to layer.
rows.locator: Section 4, Experiments on fully connected neural networks; Figure 2(a)
rows.note: The text reports similar results with a two-layer network but does not provide separate layer values.
rows.check: Layer tail-indices are measured after 10K iterations; no held-out performance or fixed-epoch batch-size penalty is reported.
